verdict.line: You lose if you trade into her Bladesurge dashes and Flawless Duet stuns before level 6; you win if you farm Q stacks, survive to 6, then flip the duel with Wither and Fury of the Sands.

brief.thesis: Irelia's kit is built to win short trades: Bladesurge (Q) dashes and heals, Flawless Duet (E) stuns and marks to refresh that dash, and Ionian Fervor stacks her attack speed every time she lands a spell — which is exactly why OP.GG grades the early lane and solo-kill edge to her. Nasus has no answer to that burst before level 6, but once Siphoning Strike stacks pile up and Fury of the Sands (R) comes online, the fight structurally reverses. That reversal is why the head-to-head win rate still sits at 51.6% over 91 games for Nasus despite the early deficit.

theirWindow.when: when her E (Flawless Duet) is up
theirWindow.what: Flawless Duet's two blades converge and stun plus Mark anyone caught between them, which instantly refreshes her Bladesurge for a follow-up dash and heal. Never stand where both blades can meet you — step to one side of the wave instead of straight down the lane.

yourWindow.when: once R (Fury of the Sands) is up
yourWindow.what: Land Wither first to decelerate her Movement and Attack Speed, drop Spirit Fire under her for the Armor reduction, then commit with Fury of the Sands active. The max-Health drain from R plus a slowed, armor-shredded Irelia is your best and safest all-in.

start.why: The 51.4% win rate over 74 games on this start reflects the sustain you need to survive Bladesurge pokes and Flawless Duet trades before your Q stacks and Fury of the Sands come online.

boots.why: Picked 52.6% of the time at a 45.9% win rate, these cut down the empowered autoattacks Irelia gets from stacking Ionian Fervor, which is most of her early damage.

core.why: The highest-performing path (63.6% over 11 games) spikes your damage right as Fury of the Sands comes online, giving you the burst to win the post-6 all-in.
Cooldown reduction and Armor directly counter the Attack Speed she gains from Ionian Fervor stacks and shortens Wither's cooldown for more frequent engages.
Boosts your Soul Eater lifesteal and healing received, letting you outlast her short trades instead of losing the extended fight.

you want a slower, more CC-heavy core path instead of Trinity Force
you want Wither and Spirit Fire up more often instead of raw Armor

runes.keystoneWhy: The extra Movement Speed and sustain on hit let you dodge Bladesurge dashes and step out of Flawless Duet's converging blades while you farm Q stacks safely.

summoners.why: This is the most-picked combo in these games (42.3% pick, 52.7% win rate) because Ghost helps you stick to or escape her Bladesurge engages while Wither is down, and Teleport lets you reset after shoving with Spirit Fire and return in time for your post-6 kill window.

playing.title: Stack Q, don't duel early
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike only grows in power when it kills its target, and at rank 1 its cooldown is 8 seconds, so before level 6 prioritize safely last-hitting minions over trading — Irelia's Bladesurge dash and Ionian Fervor stacks win a prolonged exchange.

playing.title: Don't stand between her E blades
playing.detail: Flawless Duet fires two blades that converge and deal damage, stun, and Mark anyone caught in between, which refreshes her Bladesurge for a follow-up dash. Stand to one side of the wave so you're never framed by both blades at once.

playing.title: Wither before she commits to Q
playing.detail: Wither decelerates Movement and Attack Speed over time, so land it just before she dashes in with Bladesurge — it slows her follow-up and the empowered autos she gets from Ionian Fervor stacks.

playing.title: Disengage below level 6
playing.detail: Without Fury of the Sands, a drawn-out fight favors her: Bladesurge resets off Marked or killed targets and her passive stacks attack speed on every spell hit. Take a trade only when it's a free Q stack, then back off.

playing.title: Drop Spirit Fire before committing
playing.detail: Spirit Fire is on a flat 12-second cooldown and reduces the Armor of anyone standing in it. Place it under her before your level-6 all-in so your autos and Q hit harder through the fight.

playing.title: All-in when R and W line up
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands is on a 120-second cooldown, so treat every time it's up alongside Wither as your designated kill window — this matches the read that Nasus wants to go in for kills right after level 6.

playing.title: Rush Trinity into Frozen Heart
playing.detail: The 63.6%-win Trinity Force into Frozen Heart into Spirit Visage path gives you the damage spike to punish her early aggression and the cooldown/Armor to blunt her attack-speed scaling once you're past the lane phase.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from real games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why these picks work, the trade patterns, and the timing windows — is tactical judgement layered on top of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Always keep your distance and pay attention to Irelia’s (P) and Conqueror stack count. Focus foremost on raising your [Q] stacks, and try go in for the kill post-level 6 when Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] come off cooldown.
